description: Defines the six phases of the Book 5 TEL evaluation cycle. Each phase has strict entry/exit conditions, active operators, skip rules, and downstream handoffs.
phase_sequence: init → parse → evaluate → compose → transform → assert

phases.label: init
phases.description: Load Book 1 (FFT) kernel and Book 4 (OR) vocabulary. Assert session context. Confirm QMROOT path terminates at 0D. Verify coherence=declared. Initialize evaluation scope as empty. No TEL operators are active in this phase.
phases.exit_condition: coherence=declared; Book 1 FFT primitives available in module registry; Book 4 OR operators available if opacity expressions are expected; QMROOT 0D confirmed; evaluation scope initialized as {}
import_order: book4_opacity_revelation (OR vocabulary — required when opacity expressions present)
book3_structural_detection (SD vocabulary — required when detection expressions present)
phases.qmroot_check: 6D absent; negative rungs absent; INV-013 = 0D only
phases.scope_state: empty — no T[…] or C[…] declarations active
phases.notes: The import order is not evaluation order — it is module registry loading order. Books 3 and 4 must be loaded before any TEL expression referencing their operators can be parsed.

phases.label: parse
phases.description: Execute TEL-Σ (SyntaxCheck) on the input expression. Validate against canonical grammar (tel.syntax_map). Produce parse_tree on PASS; halt and record error_report on FAIL.
phases.entry_condition: init complete; coherence=declared; raw TEL expression string E is provided
phases.exit_condition: TEL-Σ returns PASS and parse_tree is recorded, OR TEL-Σ returns FAIL and error_report is recorded and evaluation halts

gate_logic.fail: error_report recorded → halt; expression must be corrected before re-entry

phases.drift_guard: No semantic assumptions may be made during parsing. Grammar is context-free — identifier resolution does not occur in this phase.
phases.notes: P-TEL-2 is a hard gate. Evaluation cannot proceed to P-TEL-3 without a PASS parse_tree. Partial parses are not valid inputs to TEL-Ε.

phases.label: evaluate
phases.description: Execute TEL-Ε (Evaluate) on the parse_tree. Apply canonical semantic evaluation rules (tel.semantics_map). Resolve all identifiers against the module registry. Execute scope lookups for symbol references. Assign structural denotations to all sub-expressions. Record any evaluation faults (EF-001 through EF-004).
phases.entry_condition: P-TEL-2 complete with PASS parse_tree; module registry loaded
phases.exit_condition: All sub-expressions have structural denotations or recorded faults; scope updated with any T[…] and C[…] declarations encountered
phases.ordering: Evaluation is inside-out (innermost parentheses first). TEL-Ε traverses the parse_tree depth-first.

fault_handling.EF-001_or_EF-002: Halt evaluation at the fault site. Do not propagate a denotation from a faulted sub-expression.
fault_handling.EF-003: Record ConstraintViolation. Halt the specific ⊢ expression. Other independent expressions may continue.
fault_handling.EF-004: Record InvariantViolation. Flag session. Evaluation may continue but session is marked tainted.

phases.notes: TEL-Ε is the semantic engine. INV-TEL-002 (Semantic Stability) requires exactly one denotation per expression. If a session produces ambiguous denotations, the implementation of TEL-Ε has a bug.

phases.label: compose
phases.description: TEL-Κ (Compose) audits the composition of compound expressions. Verifies that INV-TEL-003 (Compositionality) is satisfied at each composition site — that the compound denotation is fully determined by sub-expression denotations and the applied composition rule. Records CompositionFault if any holistic meaning contribution is detected.
phases.entry_condition: P-TEL-3 complete; all non-faulted sub-expressions have structural denotations
phases.exit_condition: All compound denotations verified as compositional; composition ordering rules (COR-001 through COR-004) verified; any CompositionFaults recorded
composition_checks: COR-001: All symbol references (#ID) resolve to prior declarations in current scope
COR-002: All parenthetical groupings are well-defined (no implicit precedence)
COR-003: INV[…] assertions appear after all their dependency expressions
COR-004: Transformation chains resolve sequentially with no forward reference violations
phases.skip_condition: May be skipped if input expression is a pure atom (no compound sub-expressions). Record skip in session audit log.
phases.notes: TEL-Κ is an auditing operator. In most implementations it runs concurrently with TEL-Ε's depth-first traversal. It is presented as a separate phase to isolate compositionality verification as a distinct responsibility.

phases.label: transform
phases.description: TEL-Τ (Transform) applies any T[ID] transformation declarations encountered during P-TEL-3/P-TEL-4. For each transformation application site (where #ID referencing a T[…] declaration appears), TEL-Τ executes the transformation and verifies INV-TEL-004 (Transformation Fidelity): valid input must produce valid output.
phases.entry_condition: P-TEL-4 complete; at least one T[ID] declaration has been encountered in the session; target structures are available
phases.exit_condition: All transformation applications have been executed and their results recorded; all EF-005 faults (if any) have been recorded against the relevant T[ID] declarations

gate_logic.fidelity_pass: valid(S) ∧ valid(S') → record PASS; S' available for downstream use
gate_logic.fidelity_fail: valid(S) ∧ ¬valid(S') → record EF-005 against T[ID]; S' must not be used downstream

phases.skip_condition: May be skipped if no T[ID] declarations were encountered in the session. Record skip in session audit log.

downstream_handoffs.book6_governance: TEL-Τ encoded regime transformations are passed to Book 6 GRL operators for enforcement evaluation
downstream_handoffs.book7_sarg: Argument structure mutations encoded in TEL-Τ are passed to Book 7 SARG defeat evaluation
downstream_handoffs.book8_nos: Identity-through-change assertions (INV-NOS-003) consume TEL-Τ outputs for philosophical grounding
downstream_handoffs.book9_pattern_dynamics: Bifurcation and mutation events in Book 9 are modelled as sequences of TEL-Τ applications

phases.notes: INV-TEL-004 is non-negotiable: if a transformation encoding produces invalidity from validity, the encoding is wrong — not the input. TEL-Τ must never suppress EF-005 and deliver a tainted transformation result.

phases.label: assert
phases.description: TEL-Α (Assert) evaluates all INV[ID]: assert e expressions and all ⊢ constraint assertion sites encountered in the session. Records PASS or InvariantViolation / ConstraintViolation. Produces the final session audit report.
phases.entry_condition: P-TEL-3, P-TEL-4, P-TEL-5 complete; all structural denotations available; all transformation results available
phases.exit_condition: All INV[…] and ⊢ sites evaluated; session audit report produced with: pass_count, violation_count, fault_log, session_status

session_status_values.clean: No faults, no violations — all assertions PASS
session_status_values.tainted: One or more EF-004 (InvariantViolation) recorded — session results are flagged
session_status_values.halted: One or more EF-001, EF-002, or EF-003 caused evaluation to halt — session is incomplete

phases.skip_condition: May be skipped if no INV[…] expressions and no ⊢ sites appear in the session. Record skip in session audit log.
phases.notes: The assert phase is the final gate of every TEL session. A session must not be reported as complete without a P-TEL-6 result. Downstream consumers (Books 6, 7, 8, 9) must check the session_status before using TEL evaluation results.

phase_diagram.sequence: init → parse → evaluate → compose → transform → assert
phase_diagram.session_audit_log: Written during all phases. Must be available to session consumer at end of P-TEL-6.
